newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU commission agrees advance beef sector payments.
newsitem.headline: EU commission agrees advance beef sector payments.

text.p: The European Commission approved on Wednesday advance payments of about 500 million Ecus worth of beef premiums from the 1996 budget which were due in 1997, a Commission offical said.
"The Commission has adopted the proposal which will be put to the beef management committee on Friday," the official said.
The draft regulation will, after the management committee has given its opinion, be published by October 1 to permit payment from that date, the official said.
The plan allows an increase in the amount of the advance payment of the beef special premium and of the suckler cow premium in addition to earlier payment.

The amended regulation states that "the advance on the special (beef) premium and on the suckler cow premium in respect of the 1996 calendar year may be paid from 1 October 1996 for an amount up to 80 percent of those premia."

The decision, which will come into force on the day it is published in the EU Official Journal, will give the Commission an additional 500 million Ecus in 1997 which farm ministers meeting in Killarney on Monday said they want used to provide additional aid to the beef sector.
The decision reflects a German-led view among ministers that the Commission's plans to cut arable area aid and set-aside aid payments are unnecessary, the official said.

A decision on Agriculture Commissioner Franz Fischler's package of measures to reform the beef sector, which he says will cost 1.3 billion Ecus, was deferred at this month's farm ministers' meeting because the European Parliament had not given an opinion.
The package will be discussed by ministers at their next meeting in Luxembourg in October.
